children.author: frogblast
children.text:
I haven’t used DS models myself to have an opinion on quality, but I have used GLM5.3 briefly and my first impressions were good. So any statements below on quality are totally speculative.

But moren concretely on the hosting side DeepSeek’s claim to faim is massively shrinking the per-user memory footprint, enabling many more concurrent users in your fixed hardware footprint. That’s why it is so cheap to host.

Having more concurrent users leads to much higher overall throughput on that same hardware. See table 2 in this article to see the tradeoffs of overall throughput vs per user latency as an example.

Deepseek would let you host higher concurrency than GLM.

Presumably that compression doesn’t come for free on the quality side.

If you’ve got a small enough user count, perhaps there are tradeoffs in DeepSeek that are not buying you anything.

GB300 DGX. Each with 256 GiB of RAM and a price of $100k?

For an enterprise, that price seems doable. But if you want 50-100 tps like Claude does, and you only have 10 users, maybe you're not an enterprise.

To pull a recent analogy, I guess we're still at the early Model S stage of LLMs.

children.author: hkalbasi
children.text: Assuming the DGX priced at $100K, and GLM-5.3 at $1.4/M output token, this has ROI of ~7 years at maximum utilization (unlikely) and ignoring operational expenses like electricity. Which makes it economically unreasonable unless you want privacy or something like that.
